artifact.summary: build_circuit(instance) synthesizes an n-qubit unitary U from a classically given 2^n x 2^m isometry V, using column-by-column reduction. For each column c, Givens rotations on index pairs (c,i), i>c, zero the entries below the pivot. A final phase on |c> makes the pivot equal to 1. The reduction gates S satisfy S V = [I;0]. The returned circuit is U = S^dagger, so U|x>_m|0>^(n-m) = V|x>. Each Givens step is a permutation-conjugated, multi-controlled Rz-Ry-Rz rotation. Gray-code multiplexors, CNOT optimization, and the CSD and qubit-by-qubit schemes are not implemented.
register_layout: q0..q(m-1): input qubits (little-endian, q0 least significant bit of column index x)
q(m)..q(n-1): qubits that the runner prepares in |0> (ancilla-like outputs)
Basis index = sum_j q_j 2^j; column x of V is V|x>, with |x>_m on q0..q(m-1) and |0> on the rest
Example n=2, m=1: q0 is the input qubit, q1 starts in |0>

equation_mapping.code_location: build_circuit: isometry validation (V^dagger V = I) and the final inverse of the reduction circuit
equation_mapping.explanation: The returned unitary U satisfies U|x>|0..0> = V|x>, with the inputs on the low-order qubits and the other qubits in |0>. The phase is fixed per column. The runner supplies the inputs.
Parameter-counting lower bound on the CNOT count. It is not a gate-level construction and is not used in the code.

equation_mapping.code_location: build_circuit loop with _givens and _phase_fix; the final red.inverse()
equation_mapping.explanation: For each column c, G_c is built from two-level rotations on span{|c>,|i>} (i>c) and a phase on |c>. Both act only on indices >= c, so the fixed columns 0..c-1 are untouched. The returned circuit is the inverse of the product G_{2^m-1}...G_0.

Uniformly controlled rotations with Gray-code CNOT/rotation compilation are not implemented. Each rotation here is a single-pattern multi-controlled Rz/Ry (a special case of a multiplexor) built with gate.control(ctrl_state=...), with no Gray-code or Walsh-Hadamard compression.
The 2^(m+n) leading CNOT scaling is not achieved by this implementation. It uses O(2^(m+n)) multi-controlled gates, each of which compiles to many CNOTs, so no CNOT-count claim is made.

specification_changes.change: Elementary steps of the column clearing are two-level (Givens) rotations on span{|c>,|i>}. Each is a CNOT-conjugated multi-controlled Rz-Ry-Rz rotation, not Gray-code uniformly controlled Ry/Rz cascades.
specification_changes.reason: The exact angle formulas and control ordering of the cascade were not specified. The Givens form is exact, easy to verify, and keeps earlier columns fixed.

specification_changes.change: Column phases are fixed by a multi-controlled phase gate on basis state |c>, replacing the 'diagonal phase' of the sketch.
specification_changes.reason: This gives an exact V rather than V up to column-dependent phases. The global phase of the circuit is still unspecified.

specification_changes.change: CNOT-count optimization and the bound comparison are not implemented.
specification_changes.reason: The exact constants are unknown and the chosen construction is not CNOT-efficient.

specification_changes.change: The matrix V is supplied in the instance JSON as matrix_real and matrix_imag (2^n x 2^m), with the little-endian convention that the input qubits are q0..q(m-1). The code accepts any m and n with 0<=m<=n<=12 and rejects non-isometries (tolerance 1e-8) with ValueError.
specification_changes.reason: The instance parameters must define a concrete classical isometry.

assumptions: The isometry is given as a dense classical matrix; the classical angle computation uses NumPy.
The inputs occupy the low-order qubits and ancilla-like qubits are |0> (prepared by the runner).
Multi-controlled gates from gate.control are acceptable standard gates and may be transpiled to CNOTs later.
Rz-Ry-Rz in time order Rz(lam), Ry(theta), Rz(phi) realizes the SU(2) matrix [[p,q],[-conj q,conj p]].
Tolerances of 1e-12 for skipping negligible rotations and 1e-8 for isometry validation are acceptable.
unresolved_issues: The circuit is not CNOT-optimal and does not reproduce the paper's gate counts or the factor-two-from-bound claim.
The Knill/CSD and qubit-by-qubit decompositions, small-case numerical optimizations, and the Stinespring/POVM extension are not implemented.
Large n with m close to n creates very many multi-controlled gates, so synthesis and transpilation can be slow near the 12-qubit cap.
The code has not been simulated here; verification is left to the runner.

validation.detail: Circuit built and transpiled successfully; no independent correctness reference selected.
